key_insight: Injecting explicit self-awareness into VLN agents lets Vision-Language Models reason about the agent's own state (pose, belief, explored map) alongside instruction and scene, producing more interpretable and robust navigation decisions.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between opaque end-to-end VLM action prediction and explicit map-based planning by making the relationships among agent, instruction, and scene explicit—addressing ambiguity, partial observability, and lack of explainability in VLN.
method: Self-awareness module that maintains an explicit agent state and belief (pose, explored map, uncertainty) during navigation.
Fuse agent belief with visual observations and instruction embeddings in a VLM-based reasoner to predict actions and generate grounded explanations.
Train with auxiliary losses (e.g., map reconstruction, instruction grounding) and expose interpretable representations (belief maps, attention maps) for heuristic planning and debugging.
impact: Enables more reliable, debuggable VLN agents useful for embodied AI and robotics; improves robustness to ambiguous instructions and provides traceable decisions for safety-critical navigation tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: instruction + panoramic view → self-awareness module → VLM reasoner → action + explanation
Belief/map overlay showing evolving explored map, agent pose, and planned vs. executed path
Attention/grounding heatmaps linking instruction phrases to scene regions
Performance chart (success rate / SPL) and ablation bars demonstrating gains from self-awareness and explainability
paper_title: AwareVLN: Reasoning with Self-awareness for Vision-Language Navigation
paper_authors: Wenxuan Guo, Xiuwei Xu, Yichen Liu, Xiangyu Li, Hang Yin
